filename: Accelerated heatwave trends from nonlinear land-atmosphere interactions in midlatitude humid regions.pdf
title: Accelerated heatwave trends from nonlinear land-atmosphere interactions in midlatitude humid regions
code_availability: The code for the XAI calculation and required for reproducing the main figures of this study are available at https://github.com/tiany97/HW_Nonlinear_L-A_Interaction
testbed_rationale: The study employs machine learning purely as a diagnostic attribution framework (XAI via GBR/XGBoost and SHAP decomposition) rather than developing or releasing benchmark datasets for parameterization or emulation testbeds.
pain_points: CMIP6 models systematically underestimate interaction nonlinearity (by ~85%) and activated-regime coupling slopes (by ~73%).
GCM structural biases in simulating initial soil moisture (too dry at heatwave onset) and sluggish soil moisture depletion rate (1.4%/day in CMIP6 vs 2.4%/day in ERA5).
Internal variability cannot explain model biases: reanalysis observations lie entirely outside the 40-member CESM2-LE ensemble spread.
extraction_notes: The ML model predicts 3-day maximum 2m temperature anomalies from 500 hPa geopotential height anomalies and surface soil moisture anomalies, and uses TreeSHAP interaction values to quantify land-atmosphere synergy.
